pageCache.text:
Welcome to Sunningwell! If you are looking for a school place for your child, please click here
Welcome to Sunningwell CE Primary School
Sunningwell is a lovely, small rural school in the heart of the Oxfordshire countryside close to the city of Oxford and the town of Abingdon. We are proud of our connections to the local community, including the church of St Leonard’s in the village and Dalton Barracks.
In January 2019 Ofsted noted that ‘Pupils enjoy learning at Sunningwell. They appreciate the many opportunities offered by the broad and balanced curriculum (and that they) thrive in many areas of the curriculum, such as drama, music and physical education (PE). Pupils … like school because of the teachers and the lessons.’ It also noted that ‘Pupils demonstrate high levels of empathy, kindness and respect for each other, staff and visitors’. At the end of KS2 children have regularly performed above national averages in reading writing and maths.
The staff at Sunningwell are dedicated, knowledgeable, caring and enthusiastic ensuring that teaching and learning are of the highest quality and fun! We are well supported by our parents and an active governing body who ‘bring a breadth of expertise, commitment and enthusiasm to their roles’ Ofsted Jan 2019.
We have a well-equipped playground and wildlife areas including a pond and a wooded spinney which are the focus of many science and outdoor lessons. We are working with the Abingdon Area Archaeological and Historical Society to excavate the footings of a Tudor cottage in our Spinney and have enjoyed association with Heritage Opera and Opera Anywhere.
Sports provision is an important part of the school’s curriculum. The school has held the Sainsbury’s Platinum Mark for School Games since 2017. We have a number of very active sports teams and encourage all of our children to participate in a wide range of sports. After school clubs run every day including sports, art and IT.
I would urge prospective parents to visit the school and to read our Ofsted report which can be found under ‘Key Information’.
‘The school’s curriculum is broad and aims to help all pupils, including those with special educational needs and/or disabilities (SEND), to learn and achieve. This is especially so in reading and mathematics.’
‘Pupils enjoy their learning. They answer questions confidently. They are eager to discuss their thoughts and reasons with each other. Classrooms are orderly as teachers insist on positive behaviour.’
‘Pupils feel safe. They trust adults to help them if they are worried. Pupils are kind and courteous to one another. Routines and expectations are well established so pupils work attentively in lessons and the school is calm.’

pageCache.text:
Here at Sunningwell we pride ourselves on the fact that we care and nuture service children from the nearby Dalton Barracks. We have a long standing attachment to the “Little Troopers” who currently form over one third of our school. We have a dedicated member of staff who currently holds the position of Service Pupils Champion as set out in the “Service Pupil Promise” held with Oxfordshire County Council. The “Little Troopers” themselves have representation on the School Parliament and hold active parts in all elements of the school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Admission Arrangements - Sunningwell Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
We would love to welcome you to our school! We warmly invite prospective parents to consider our primary school for their children. Visits to look round the school while ‘in action’ are welcomed and can easily be arranged by calling the School Office (01865 739378) to arrange a mutually suitable appointment time.
Oxfordshire County Council – general admissions information
For up-to-date information about School Admissions, please use the following link to the Oxfordshire County Council Website: Oxfordshire County Council Admission Rules and Oxfordshire County Council Apply for a School Place.
Admission Arrangements
Administration of admission arrangements to County Primary Schools is dealt with centrally by Oxfordshire County Council.
Starting school for the first time (Reception admissions)
You can apply for a reception school place through Oxfordshire County Council’s website.
Starting school is a very important time for you, your child and the school. We all work together to make the transition smooth. In the term prior to their entry, pupils are invited into school for a visit. This will help your child become familiar with the surroundings and routines of school. During this period, there will be a meeting for parents, to discuss our partnership with you.
Deferring entry to Reception
Some parents may believe it is in their child’s best interests to delay entry to an infant and primary school. Parents of children born between 1 April and 31 August can request that their application be delayed to the September following their child’s 5th birthday instead of the September before their child’s 5th birthday. You can find more information on deferring a school place here.
Joining the school later on
Sometimes children join the school later in their school life, often transferring from another school. Oxfordshire County Council manage these admissions. You can find more information on this page of their website.
We make every effort to ensure they are welcomed, looked after, and monitored so that they quickly make friends and can find their way around the school. Teachers give children time to settle in before assessing their academic abilities. This assessment, together with records from the previous school, will enable your child to have the best start in our school. Parents and carers are asked to contact the school if their child has difficulty settling.
Admission numbers & appeals
Every effort is made to make a place available for your child in our school. However, schools have a limit on the number of children they can take. In the case of Sunningwell CE Primary School the Published Admissions Number (PAN) is 15 in each year group. This figure is set by the Local Authority (LA) and agreed with Governors and Headteacher. If the number of children wanting a place is below the set figure, your child will be offered a place. There may, however, come a point when there are too many children of that year group for them all to be given a place. Oxfordshire County Council determine an over-subscription criterion, outlining the procedure for awarding places when oversubscribed. You can find the information here.
If a place is not available on application, you have the right to appeal to Oxfordshire County Council Education Authority. Appeals are heard by an independent panel. A Guide to Admission Appeals can be obtained from the Admissions Team via the County Council website (above).
Moving on – transferring to Secondary school
Sunningwell CE Primary School is part of the Abingdon Partnership of Schools. We have strong links with many of the schools in the local area, including the secondary schools. Our children may visit these schools for sports and other activities which enables them to become familiar with the sites. In addition transition days take place in the term before children move into Year 7 and additional days are put in place where there is a need. To apply for secondary school places in Oxfordshire, please following this link https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/schools/apply-school-place/year-7-applications
